technical_requirements: Throughput targets: 12k tokens/sec sustained per region for reranking fleet, burst to 50k tokens/sec for global peak windows. Latency: p95 <= 120ms for reranking, p95 <= 200ms for chat when serving <= 80% of reserved capacity. Failover headroom: require at least 25% warm capacity in N+1 region; option to increase to 35% during holiday season. Preferred instance profile: A100-40GB or equivalent; support for int8/4 quantized variants. KV cache warming strategy required for fast failover; expectation of symmetric model deployment in at least two AZs per region.
reserved_capacity_plan: Requested blueprint (customer-provided): Primary region (us-east-1): 24 reserved GPUs (12 for rerank/embeddings, 12 for chat/interactive). Secondary region (us-west-2): 10 reserved GPUs as warm-standby (can take 25% of primary load on failover). Europe (eu-west-1): 12 reserved GPUs to serve EU traffic + residency. Total initial commit: 46 reserved GPUs across 3 regions. Customer open to burst credits for short spikes. Wants explicit network egress caps and locality-routing policy in contract. SE recommended Dedicated pools per region with cross-region failover policy and automated pre-warm of KV caches during failover.
sla_expectations: Customer expects 99.9% regional uptime with RTO <= 60s for automated failover to warm-standby region for stateless reranking; RTO <= 120s for stateful chat sessions (with partial degradation allowed). Penalty language requested for multi-hour outages. Also requesting monthly reports (latency percentiles, token throughput, cache hit rates) and quarterly capacity planning review. Redwood to provide explicit runbooks for failover testing and an annual DR rehearsal window.
